title: Decentralized learning leaderboard
notice: Non-IID comparison: tune each algorithm independently on Dirichlet alpha 0.1 validation data with homogeneous hardware. Joint TPE search over learning rate and H in {1, 5, 10, 15, 20}; DeMo also tunes residual decay, DCT block size and coefficients per block (H is gradient accumulation for DeMo). Each algorithm receives 40 configurations, three paired seeds and full 900-second budgets. Freeze all winning parameters and the shared checkpoint for all four evaluation settings. New campaigns use three workers per GPU. Archived IID campaigns are excluded. DeMo is queued after the complete Epidemic Learning campaign.

algorithms.label: dpsgd-kreg-log2
algorithms.description: Each client learns from its own data for a small number of minibatch updates, exchanges its model with five neighbors, and averages the received models with its own. Repeating this spreads learning through the network without a central server.
steps: Perform H local SGD updates with minibatches of 32 examples.
Send the resulting model to each of the five fixed neighbors.
Wait for every neighbor’s model from the same round, then average all six models equally.
Begin the next local round; there is no global barrier.

paper.title: Can Decentralized Algorithms Outperform Centralized Algorithms? A Case Study for Decentralized Parallel Stochastic Gradient Descent
paper.authors: Xiangru Lian, Ce Zhang, Huan Zhang, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Wei Zhang, Ji Liu

algorithms.implementation_note: This repository implements the train-then-average variant: x_next = W LocalSGD(x, H). At H = 1 this is W(x − ηg(x)); Algorithm 1 of the original paper uses Wx − ηg(x). The benchmark therefore measures this declared variant, not an exact reproduction of that algorithm.

algorithms.label: shatter-k16-rlog2
algorithms.description: Each real node trains its own model, divides it into 16 chunks, and exchanges those chunks through 16 virtual nodes. The 512 virtual nodes form a new random 5-regular graph each round. Each real node combines received chunks with its own to build the model for its next local training block.
steps: Train H local SGD minibatches on each of the 32 real nodes.
Flatten the model state into 16 contiguous chunks; retain any remainder in the last chunk.
Draw the round’s seeded 5-regular graph over 512 virtual nodes. Each virtual node sends its assigned chunk along its five graph edges.
Wait for the same-round incoming chunks. Average each chunk index over its received copies and the real node’s own copy, then reconstruct the model.
Publish the reconstructed model and start the next local block. Virtual nodes share their real node’s bandwidth and compute resources.

algorithms.label: epidemic-kreg-log2
algorithms.description: Each of 32 real nodes trains locally, exchanges its full model with five neighbors, and averages the received models with its own. A fresh random 5-regular graph is drawn each round, so information travels through changing neighborhoods.
steps: Perform H local SGD updates with minibatches of 32 examples.
Draw the round’s seeded random 5-regular graph over the 32 real nodes.
Send the full trained model to each of the five neighbors.
Wait for all five same-round neighbor models and average them with the local model using equal weights.
Publish the averaged model and begin the next local block; there is no global round barrier.

algorithms.label: DeMo
algorithms.description: Each client accumulates gradients at the shared model, adds them to its private compression residual, and sends the largest DCT coefficients. A ring all-gather delivers every client packet; clients reconstruct the shared update and take a sign step.
steps: Average H minibatch gradients at fixed model parameters; H does not perform local SGD updates.
Decay the private residual and add learning-rate-scaled gradients; transform into DCT blocks and retain the largest coefficients by magnitude.
Subtract the locally transmitted reconstruction from the residual, retaining unsent information for future rounds.
Run a 31-stage ring all-gather across 32 clients; charge packet indices, values, headers, physical bandwidth and per-transfer latency.
Average transmitted coefficients at collisions, reconstruct the update and take a learning-rate-scaled sign step. Publish locally after all packets arrive.

paper.title: DeMo: Decoupled Momentum Optimization
paper.authors: Bowen Peng, Jeffrey Quesnelle, Diederik P. Kingma (original 2024 release)

algorithms.author_code_note: The authors’ repository identifies this as supplementary material for DeMo and provides the standalone demo.py optimizer.
algorithms.implementation_note: Existing reference-style Signum DeMo with private residuals and an explicit directed ring all-gather. H is fixed-weight gradient accumulation, not H local model updates. The ring is a benchmark transport choice; this is not a reproduction of the paper’s language-model experiments.

parameter_notes.role: Jointly tuned. DeMo uses sign updates, so its learning-rate range is declared separately from plain SGD; it includes the earlier 0.001 baseline.
Jointly tuned. Gradients are averaged over H minibatches at unchanged parameters; compute time charges all H minibatches.
Jointly tuned. Controls persistence of untransmitted information; separate from SGD momentum, which stays zero.
Jointly tuned maximum transform size per tensor dimension; actual block dimensions divide the tensor shape.
Jointly tuned top-k coefficient count, clipped to each actual block’s coefficient count. This is a count, not a percentage; actual packet bytes are charged.

parameter_notes.value: Fixed directed ring i → (i+1) mod 32; 31 stages
parameter_notes.role: All packets reach every node. Physical endpoint capacities are shared; no free broadcast or independent virtual bandwidth.

parameter_notes.parameter: Batch size / SGD momentum / weight decay
parameter_notes.role: Fixed. DeMo’s compression residual is tuned independently; no additional SGD momentum.
Two configurations × three paired seeds per batch; starts after all Epidemic Learning tuning and evaluations succeed.

parameter_notes.value: 20 ms per minibatch; 1,000,000 bytes/s; 10 ms transfer latency
parameter_notes.role: Same capacities as other campaigns. DCT, compression and reconstruction add no modeled compute time; measured execution wall time is reported separately.

limitations: Tuning on one scenario measures parameter transfer, not each scenario’s separately tuned optimum.
Forty configurations are a finite joint search over five parameters, not an exhaustive search or global optimum.
Gradient accumulation and sign updates differ from the local-SGD update rule of the other algorithms; H has an algorithm-specific meaning.
The ring all-gather requires stable membership and can be limited by slow participants and its 31 transfer stages.
The evaluation is an offline, uniformly averaged global model; collection and evaluation costs are excluded from simulated protocol time.
Compression compute costs are excluded from simulated protocol time; the network uses greedy endpoint scheduling and additive delivery latency.
The CIFAR-10 test set was examined in previous campaigns; these evaluations remain exploratory.
No previous scores or winning parameters are imported; the earlier DeMo runs motivate only the declared search range.
